elk.title: Elk
elk.description: Elk appear in Emerald Lake and Asgard Mountain. Search forest and mountain habitats; Gimli Ridge is not one of their listed areas.

mule-deer.title: Mule Deer
mule-deer.description: Mule deer occupy forest and clearing habitats in Emerald Lake and Gimli Ridge. They are one of the common mammals to watch for between cabin stops.

kokanee-salmon.title: Kokanee Salmon
kokanee-salmon.description: Look in the rivers and lakes of Emerald Lake and Asgard Mountain for Kokanee salmon. Dry weather is listed, with sightings possible in both daytime and night.

common-raven.title: Common Raven
common-raven.description: Ravens are found across Canada’s three areas, in forests and mountain habitats. They offer a bird subject to watch for while working through the higher trails.

red-fox.title: Red Fox
red-fox.description: Red foxes have locations in Emerald Lake and Asgard Mountain. Keep an eye on forest and clearing habitats as the route leaves open mountain ground.

moose.title: Moose
moose.description: Moose appear in forest and wetland habitats in Emerald Lake and Gimli Ridge. Both day and night are listed, and either dry or wet weather can fit the search.

black-bear.title: Black Bear
black-bear.description: Black bears can appear in the forests of Emerald Lake and Gimli Ridge. They are rare, with both daytime and night listed as active periods in dry weather.

gray-wolf.title: Gray Wolf
gray-wolf.description: Gray wolves are a night-time forest subject in Emerald Lake and Asgard Mountain. Both dry and wet conditions are listed for this uncommon animal.

coyote.title: Coyote
coyote.description: Coyotes have locations in Emerald Lake and Gimli Ridge. Watch forest edges and clearings in dry weather, with both day and night listed as active periods.

beaver.title: Beaver
beaver.description: Beavers are a night-time river search across all three Canadian areas. A daytime pass along the same water may leave this Compendium entry unfinished.

canada-goose.title: Canada Goose
canada-goose.description: Check the wetlands and lakes of Emerald Lake and Gimli Ridge during the day. Dry weather is the listed condition for this water bird.

sasquatch.title: Sasquatch
sasquatch.description: Sasquatch is a legendary, night-time Emerald Lake subject. Remote Forest is its habitat label; it does not define a guaranteed distance from a cabin or a reliable spawn trick.

mountain-goat.title: Mountain Goat
mountain-goat.description: Mountain goats are found in Gimli Ridge and Asgard Mountain. Their mountain habitat puts this daytime photography target alongside the steeper Canadian routes.

bighorn-sheep.title: Bighorn Sheep
bighorn-sheep.description: Look on forested mountain terrain in Gimli Ridge and Asgard Mountain. This is a different Compendium entry from Algeria’s Barbary sheep.

bald-eagle.title: Bald Eagle
bald-eagle.description: Scan the lakes and cliffs of Gimli Ridge and Asgard Mountain for this large bird. Keep it in view as you line up the camera rather than driving straight toward it.

grizzly-bear.title: Grizzly Bear
grizzly-bear.description: Grizzlies have locations in Gimli Ridge and Asgard Mountain. Search remote forest, river and lake habitats during the day in dry weather.

barbary-sheep.title: Barbary Sheep (Aoudad)
barbary-sheep.description: The rocky slopes of both Algerian areas are home to the aoudad. Mountain and rock habitats are the places to check when the desert floor is quiet.

egyptian-vulture.title: Egyptian Vulture
egyptian-vulture.description: This rare bird has locations in both Algerian areas. Watch cliff and sand habitats during the day, with dry weather as its listed condition.

desert-sparrow.title: Desert Sparrow
desert-sparrow.description: The desert sparrow is a small bird associated with oasis and sand habitats. Check both Algerian areas rather than mistaking this entry for a Canadian bird.

lanner-falcon.title: Lanner Falcon
lanner-falcon.description: Lanner falcons have locations in both Algerian areas. Mountain and cliff habitats in dry daytime conditions are the places to watch for this uncommon bird.

dromedary-camel.title: Dromedary Camel
dromedary-camel.description: Dromedaries belong to the Tassili n’Ajjer Desert area. Check its sand and oasis habitats before heading into the Aurès Mountains for a different animal.

fennec-fox.title: Fennec Fox
fennec-fox.description: The fennec fox has locations in Tassili n’Ajjer Desert. Check river and sand habitats in dry weather; its active period includes both daytime and night.

saharan-cheetah.title: Saharan Cheetah
saharan-cheetah.description: The Saharan cheetah is a legendary Tassili n’Ajjer Desert animal. Its area and conditions matter more than searching every Algerian landscape without a plan.

striped-hyena.title: Striped Hyena
striped-hyena.description: Striped hyenas can appear in both Algerian areas. Plan around their night-time activity and check the listed weather before starting the search.

jackal.title: Jackal
jackal.description: Jackals are a night-time photography target in the Aurès Mountains. Keep that area requirement in mind when planning a trip for Algeria’s smaller mammals.

flamingo.title: Flamingo
flamingo.description: Head to the oases of the Aurès Mountains for flamingos. This daytime bird needs dry conditions and is a separate Compendium entry from Algeria’s sparrows, falcons and vultures.

dorcas-gazelle.title: Dorcas Gazelle
dorcas-gazelle.description: The Aurès Mountains are the confirmed area for Dorcas gazelles. Search river, oasis and sand habitats in dry weather; both day and night are listed.
